description:
You are the artifact repository administrator at Nexus Financial, a capital markets firm. A new application project called 'TradeX Platform' has been kicked off and the development team lead has requested a complete Artifactory setup before the first sprint begins. The following six deliverables must all be in place:

1. A local generic repository named 'tradex-artifacts' (description: 'TradeX Platform build artifacts') to store binary deliverables, configuration bundles, and build outputs that do not fit a typed package format.
2. A local Maven repository named 'tradex-maven-releases' (description: 'TradeX Java release artifacts') for the Java microservice release JARs produced by the TradeX build pipeline.
3. A group named 'tradex-developers' for all engineers assigned to the TradeX project.
4. A permission target named 'tradex-dev-perms' that grants the 'tradex-developers' group Admin, Deploy, Annotate, and Read privileges on both 'tradex-artifacts' and 'tradex-maven-releases'. Both repositories must be in the permission scope — not just one.
5. An access token for the admin user with description 'TradeX CI/CD production token' to be used by the production deployment pipeline.
6. Upload the file /home/ga/Desktop/commons-io-2.15.1.jar to the 'tradex-artifacts' repository as the project's initial dependency artifact.

All six deliverables must be completed before the team's kickoff on Monday. Artifactory is at http://localhost:8082 (admin / password).
